property_summary: For every admissible input where all external calls from transfer succeed, C.transfer always returns true; the mutant returns false even when calls succeed, so it violates this rule for some inputs.

For any non-empty _tos array and a callee that always succeeds on the encoded transferFrom call, the reference C.transfer returns true (the mutant returns false), so assert that calling transfer completes and returns true for such inputs.

For any non-empty _tos array and a callee that always succeeds on the encoded transferFrom call, C.transfer(...) always completes and returns true; the mutant returns false for the same successful-callee scenario, breaking this rule.

For any non-empty _tos array and a callee that successfully handles the encoded transferFrom calls, C.transfer(...) always returns true; the mutant returns false for some such inputs, so the invariant 'transfer returns true when all external calls succeed' is broken by the mutant.

For any non-empty _tos array and a callee contract that always succeeds on the encoded transferFrom calls, C.transfer(...) returns true (the mutant returns false for the same inputs), so the reference always returns true while the mutant can return false.

For any inputs with a non-empty _tos array and a callee that can both succeed and fail, the reference C always returns true (call completes) when the external calls succeed, whereas the mutant inverts the success check and will revert whenever an external call succeeds — so there exists inputs (a callee that succeeds and at least one _tos element) that make the mutant revert while the reference returns true.
